item.title: Ichigoni: Aomori's Luxurious Sea Urchin Soup — Guide
item.description: Ichigoni is a luxurious clear soup of sea urchin and abalone from the Hachinohe coast. Its name — ‘strawberry simmer’ — comes from the way the milky, poached sea urchin resembles wild strawberries floating in the broth. A summer delicacy, it’s one of Aomori’s most special regional dishes. 🗓️ At a Glance Location Hachinohe & Sanriku coast, Aomori Hours Restaurant hours (seasonal) Admission Premium; varies Time needed About 1 hour Best time Summer (urchin season) What to Try Clear, delicate sea urchin and abalone soup.

item.title: Sanriku Seafood & Sea Urchin: Iwate's Coastal Feast — Guide
item.description: The Sanriku coast’s complex ria shoreline creates Japan’s richest marine nursery — Iwate’s uni (sea urchin), awabi (abalone), kaki (oyster) and salmon are among the finest in the country. Miyako’s morning market and the harbour restaurants of Kamaishi and Ofunato serve them fresh at a fraction of Tokyo prices. 🗓️ At a Glance Location Sanriku coast (Miyako etc.), Iwate Hours Market mornings; restaurant hours Admission Varies by dish Time needed About 1 hour Best time Uni summer; oysters winter What to Try Fresh sea urchin (uni) bowls in summer.

item.title: Shakotan Peninsula Guide: Cape Kamui, Blue Sea & Uni
item.description: West of Otaru, the rugged Shakotan Peninsula is famous for one thing above all: the colour of its sea. The vivid, jewel-like “Shakotan Blue” glows beneath dramatic cliffs and capes, making this one of Hokkaido’s most beautiful stretches of coast and its only marine park. Walk out to wild Cape Kamui and Cape Shimamui for sweeping ocean views, then feast on the region’s celebrated summer sea urchin (uni), served gloriously fresh on rice.
